seo.title: About Us
seo.description: Hirani Law Firm PLLC is built on one principle: your case is personal. Learn about our client-first approach to family law and personal injury in Greater Houston.

intro.title: A law firm built on one powerful principle.
paragraphs: We believe every client deserves a dedicated team committed to protecting their rights and securing their future. We are more than just your lawyers — we are your partners and your advocates during life's most difficult chapters.
Whether you are navigating a divorce, fighting for child custody, pursuing a personal injury claim, or handling an adoption, Hirani Law Firm brings the same commitment: your case is personal to us.

aboutPage.quote: You deserve a legal team that knows your name, understands your struggle, and is personally committed to your success.

mission.title: A Client-First Approach to Law
mission.description: Our mission is simple: to provide exceptional legal representation that eases the emotional and financial burden on our clients. The "Hirani Law Firm difference" is our unwavering commitment to a client-first approach. This means we prioritize:

cards.title: Clear Communication
cards.description: Keeping you informed and empowered at every stage of your case — no jargon, no unanswered calls.

cards.title: Compassionate Guidance
cards.description: Understanding the human side of your struggle and providing the support you need through family law and personal injury matters.

cards.title: Aggressive Representation
cards.description: Fighting relentlessly in negotiations and in the courtroom to achieve the best possible outcome for you and your family.

values.title: Founded out of a belief that legal representation should be personal.
values.description: Attorney Sehar Hirani founded Hirani Law Firm in 2018 out of a frustration with the impersonal, volume-based nature of many larger firms. She envisioned a practice where every client's case is treated with the urgency and personal attention it deserves. This vision is the foundation of our core values:

cards.title: Integrity
cards.description: We uphold the highest ethical standards, ensuring our actions are always aligned with your best interests.

cards.title: Empathy
cards.description: We understand that behind every case are real people with real concerns. We approach every situation with the compassion and understanding it deserves.

cards.title: Tenacity
cards.description: We are relentless in our pursuit of justice for our clients. We do not back down from a fight when our clients' futures are on the line.

difference.eyebrow: What It Means To Work With Us
difference.title: When you choose Hirani Law Firm, you are choosing a different kind of legal experience.

cards.title: Clarity and Transparency

cards.title: Compassion and Strength

seo.description: Attorney Sehar Hirani — Family Law & Personal Injury attorney licensed in Texas since 2018. A mother, an advocate, and a steady guide through life's most difficult legal moments.

hero.name: Sehar Hirani
subtitle: Family Law & Personal Injury Attorney
Licensed in Texas Since 2018
hero.description: A mother of two, an advocate for families, and a steady guide through some of life's most difficult legal moments — Sehar Hirani brings both personal understanding and practiced legal skill to every case she takes on. She founded Hirani Law Firm to give clients the personal attention, honest communication, and determined advocacy that larger, volume-based firms too often overlook. When you work with Sehar, you work directly with an attorney who treats your case as if it were her own family's.

sections.title: A Practice Built on Compassion and Personal Connection
paragraphs: Sehar Hirani is a mom of two, and that perspective shapes the way she serves families. She understands that divorce, custody, support, adoption, and enforcement matters can affect a client's children, home, finances, and sense of stability all at once. When you sit across from Sehar, you are not talking to someone who has only read about these challenges in a textbook — you are talking to someone who understands what is at stake.

She believes strongly in father's rights and in defending fathers who want to remain present and active in their children's lives. Her work is guided by a deep passion for children and family, and by the belief that every parent deserves to be heard with dignity and represented with skill.

quote.text: Clients often come to the firm during a painful or uncertain season. My goal is to make sure they leave every meeting feeling clearer, steadier, and more prepared for what comes next.
quote.author: Sehar Hirani

strategy.title: Sensitive Approach, Strategic Thinking
paragraphs: Sehar uses a sensitive approach that balances genuine compassion with clear legal direction. She helps clients understand the process and prepare for the decisions ahead — not just emotionally, but strategically. Every case receives a legal plan built around the client's specific family, timeline, and goals.

While she always works to reach amicable resolutions, she is fully prepared to be a fierce advocate in mediation or in the courtroom when the other party refuses to be reasonable. Every case is prepared as if it will go to trial — which gives clients maximum leverage at every stage.

education.title: Education, Credentials & Local Court Experience
paragraphs: Sehar graduated from the University of Houston and South Texas College of Law. She has been licensed in the State of Texas since 2018 and is an active member of the State Bar of Texas, the Family Law Section of the State Bar of Texas, the Houston Bar Association, and the Fort Bend County Bar Association.
Her family law practice covers Harris, Fort Bend, Montgomery, Galveston, Austin, Waller, and Liberty counties. Personal injury cases may be handled throughout the State of Texas.

seo.description: Hirani Law Firm provides family law and personal injury representation across Greater Houston — Harris, Fort Bend, Montgomery, Galveston, Austin, Waller, and Liberty counties.

intro.eyebrow: Deeply Rooted In The Communities We Serve
intro.title: Local knowledge. Powerful advantage.
paragraphs: From our central office in Katy, Hirani Law Firm provides dedicated legal representation across the Greater Houston area. We believe that a successful case often depends on having a local attorney who understands your community and your court. We are that law firm. We are committed to being that trusted legal partner for our entire community.

Being a local law firm means more than just having an office here; it means understanding the communities we serve. Attorney Sehar Hirani has built her practice on a deep familiarity with the local legal landscape. We understand the specific nuances of the different court systems, the procedures of the local judges, and the values that matter to the families in this region. This local knowledge is a powerful advantage, allowing us to provide tailored and effective legal strategies for your case.

areas.title: Comprehensive legal support across all our service areas.

counties.name: Harris County
counties.description: As the region's largest county, Harris County's legal system can be complex to navigate. Our attorneys have significant experience advocating for clients at the Harris County Family Law Center, confidently handling the unique procedures and pace of Houston's busy courts. We proudly serve clients in Houston, Pasadena, Cypress, Spring, Tomball, and all surrounding communities.

counties.name: Fort Bend County
counties.description: Based in the heart of Fort Bend County, our firm has a strong presence in the local community. We regularly represent our neighbors, navigating the specific procedures of the Fort Bend County courts in Richmond with confidence and skill. We serve clients across Sugar Land, Richmond, Rosenberg, Missouri City, and, of course, our home base of Katy.

counties.name: Montgomery County
counties.description: We serve families throughout Montgomery County, bringing the same dedicated advocacy to clients in the rapidly growing communities north of Houston. We understand the local courts and provide the same client-first approach to every family we represent in this region, from The Woodlands to Conroe.

counties.name: Galveston County
counties.description: We extend our commitment to serving Texas families all the way to the Gulf Coast. If you have a family law or personal injury case in Galveston County, you can expect the same high level of dedicated advocacy we provide to all our clients. Our service areas include Galveston, League City, Texas City, Friendswood, and Dickinson.

counties.name: Austin County
counties.description: We believe that expert legal representation should be accessible to everyone, including those in the more rural communities of our region. Hirani Law Firm is proud to serve clients throughout Austin County, including the cities of Bellville, Sealy, and Wallis.

counties.name: Waller County
counties.description: Our firm proudly extends representation to families and individuals in Waller County, ensuring that clients in the growing west Houston corridor have access to the same quality legal advocacy that defines our practice.

counties.name: Liberty County
counties.description: Hirani Law Firm serves clients in Liberty County as part of our Greater Houston family law coverage area, providing the same client-first approach to families east of the city.

counties.name: Personal Injury — All of Texas
counties.description: For personal injury matters — auto accidents, 18-wheelers, motorcycle accidents, slip and fall, and workers' compensation — Hirani Law Firm practices all over Texas. Your location is never a barrier to representation. No matter where in Texas your accident occurred, we can help.

personalInjuryPage.heroSubtitle: No fee unless we win. Contingency-based personal injury representation throughout the State of Texas.
paragraphs: Insurance companies move fast after an accident — often contacting victims before they have legal representation, hoping to settle claims for far less than they are worth. Attorney Sehar Hirani levels that playing field. She handles injury cases on a contingency basis, which means you pay nothing unless we recover compensation for you.

The firm represents injury victims throughout the State of Texas, with particular experience in the Houston and Katy area. From the first call to the final settlement or verdict, your case gets the personal attention it deserves.

seo.title: Frequently Asked Questions
seo.description: Clear answers to common questions about Texas divorce, custody, child support, CPS defense, and personal injury claims from Hirani Law Firm.

hero.title: Frequently Asked Questions
hero.description: When you're facing a serious legal issue, the uncertainty can be overwhelming. We have created this page to provide clear, straightforward answers to the most common questions we receive from clients in Houston and the surrounding areas.

items.q: What is the difference between a contested and an uncontested divorce?
items.a: An uncontested divorce is one where both spouses agree on all major issues, such as property division, child custody, and support. It is generally faster and less expensive. A contested divorce is when spouses cannot agree on one or more issues, requiring negotiation, mediation, or even a court trial to resolve the disputes.

items.q: How is property divided in a Texas divorce? Is it always 50/50?
items.a: Texas is a community property state, meaning most assets and debts acquired during the marriage belong to both spouses. However, the division is not automatically 50/50. A judge will divide the property in a "just and right" manner, which can be influenced by factors like fault in the breakup of the marriage, disparity in earning power, and the needs of the children.

items.q: What is spousal support (alimony), and who is eligible for it in Texas?
items.a: Spousal support, or alimony, is a court-ordered payment from one spouse to the other after a divorce. In Texas, it is not awarded in every case. A judge may award it if the marriage lasted 10 years or more and the requesting spouse cannot earn sufficient income, or in cases involving family violence.

items.q: How long does a divorce take in Texas?
items.a: Texas has a mandatory 60-day waiting period after a divorce petition is filed. An uncontested divorce can be finalized shortly after this period. A contested divorce can take several months to over a year to resolve, depending on the complexity and level of conflict.

items.q: Do I need a lawyer for an amicable or uncontested divorce?
items.a: Yes, it is highly recommended. Even if you and your spouse agree on everything, an attorney ensures that your rights are protected and that the final divorce decree is drafted correctly and filed properly. Mistakes in the paperwork can lead to significant legal and financial problems in the future.

items.q: What is the difference between "custody" and "conservatorship" in Texas?
items.a: In Texas, the legal term for custody is "conservatorship." It defines a parent's legal rights and responsibilities. While people often use the term "custody," all official court orders will refer to parents as "conservators."

items.q: How do Texas courts decide who gets custody? What is the "best interest of the child"?
items.a: The court's only consideration is the "best interest of the child." A judge will evaluate many factors, including the child's emotional and physical needs, the stability of each parent's home, each parent's ability to care for the child, and any history of conflict or abuse.

items.q: Do Texas courts favor mothers over fathers?
items.a: No. The law in Texas is explicitly gender-neutral. Fathers have the same legal rights as mothers, and the court cannot use gender as a factor in its decision. The outcome is based entirely on what is best for the child.

items.q: What is a Standard Possession Order (SPO)?
items.a: The Standard Possession Order is a default parenting time (visitation) schedule that is presumed to be in the child's best interest. It outlines a detailed schedule for weekends, holidays, and summer vacation for the non-primary parent.

items.q: How can I modify my current custody or visitation order?
items.a: To modify an order, you must file a formal petition with the court and prove that there has been a "material and substantial change" in the circumstances of either the parents or the child since the last order was signed.

items.q: How is child support calculated in Texas?
items.a: Child support is calculated using state guidelines, which are based on a percentage of the paying parent's net monthly resources. The percentage changes based on the number of children. For one child, it is 20%; for two, it is 25%, and so on.

items.q: What do I do if the other parent stops paying child support?
items.a: You should contact an attorney immediately to file an enforcement action. A judge can force the other parent to pay what is owed and can impose penalties, including fines and even jail time.

items.q: Can my child support amount be changed if my income changes?
items.a: Yes. If you or the other parent has experienced a significant change in income (either an increase or a decrease), you can petition the court to modify the child support order to reflect the new financial reality.

items.q: How long does child support last in Texas?
items.a: Typically, child support continues until the child turns 18 or graduates from high school, whichever occurs later. Support can be extended indefinitely if the child has a qualifying disability.

items.q: What are my rights if a CPS caseworker comes to my door?
items.a: You have the right not to let them into your home without a court order. You have the right to remain silent, and you have the right to an attorney. It is crucial to be polite but firm and to call an attorney immediately before answering any questions.

items.q: Do I have to sign a CPS Safety Plan?
items.a: No, and you should not sign any document from CPS without first consulting with an attorney. These plans often require you to give up significant legal rights, and they can be used against you in court.

items.q: Can CPS take my children without a court order?
items.a: Only in very rare emergencies where they believe a child is in immediate, imminent danger. In nearly all other cases, they must obtain a court order to legally remove a child from your home.

items.q: How can I fight false allegations from CPS?
items.a: The best way to fight false allegations is to hire an experienced CPS defense attorney immediately. Your attorney will challenge the evidence, present your side of the story, and hold CPS accountable to the high legal standard required to interfere with your family.

items.q: What should I do immediately after a car accident?
items.a: First, ensure everyone is safe and seek medical attention, even for seemingly minor injuries. Second, call the police to create an official report. Third, document the scene by taking pictures of the vehicles, the area, and your injuries. Finally, do not admit fault and contact a personal injury attorney before speaking with any insurance companies.

items.q: How long do I have to file a personal injury claim in Texas?
items.a: In Texas, the statute of limitations for most personal injury claims is two years from the date of the injury. If you do not file a lawsuit within this timeframe, you will likely lose your right to recover any compensation.

items.q: What evidence is most important for my personal injury claim?
items.a: Key evidence includes the police report, photos and videos of the accident scene and your injuries, contact information for any witnesses, all of your medical records and bills, and documentation of any lost wages.

items.q: Should I talk to the other party's insurance company?
items.a: It is not recommended. The other party's insurance adjuster is trained to get you to say things that can hurt your claim. It is always best to let your attorney handle all communication with insurance companies.

items.q: How much is my personal injury case worth?
items.a: The value of your case depends on many factors, including the severity of your injuries, the total cost of your medical treatment, the amount of lost income, and the impact on your quality of life. An experienced attorney can evaluate these factors to give you an estimate of your case's value.

items.q: What types of damages can I recover?
items.a: You can recover "economic" damages, such as medical bills and lost wages, and "non-economic" damages, such as compensation for pain and suffering, emotional distress, and physical impairment.

items.q: How does a personal injury lawyer get paid?
items.a: Most personal injury lawyers, including Hirani Law Firm, work on a contingency fee basis. This means we only get paid if we win your case, either through a settlement or a court verdict. Our fee is a percentage of the total recovery, so you pay nothing up front.

items.q: Will my case go to trial, or will it settle?
items.a: The vast majority of personal injury cases are resolved through a settlement with the insurance company. However, if the insurance company refuses to make a fair offer, we are always prepared to take your case to trial to fight for the compensation you deserve.

items.q: How long does it take to resolve a personal injury case?
items.a: The timeline varies. A straightforward case that settles can be resolved in a matter of months. A more complex case that requires a lawsuit and goes to trial can take a year or more.

items.q: What if I were partially at fault for the accident?
items.a: Texas follows a "modified comparative fault" rule. This means you can still recover damages as long as you are not found to be 51% or more at fault. However, your recovery will be reduced by your percentage of fault.

items.q: What happens if the at-fault driver doesn't have insurance?
items.a: If you have Uninsured/Underinsured Motorist (UM/UIM) coverage on your own auto insurance policy, you can file a claim with your own insurance company to cover your damages.

items.q: Can I sue for a slip and fall accident on someone else's property?
items.a: Yes. Property owners have a legal duty to keep their premises reasonably safe. If you were injured due to an unsafe condition that the owner knew or should have known about, you may have a valid premises liability claim.

items.q: What is a wrongful death claim, and who can file one?
items.a: A wrongful death claim can be filed when a person's death is caused by the negligence or wrongful act of another. In Texas, these claims can typically be filed by the deceased's surviving spouse, children, and parents.
